issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). However, the solution repository declares Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return boolean and the Seal/Goat implementations return boolean (printing the message instead). This contradicts the exercise specification and will confuse students about the expected return type and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Milkable interface and its implementations to match the specification: declare messageOnMilk() to return String, and have implementations return the milk message String (e.g., "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Update Seal.java and Goat.java accordingly so their messageOnMilk() returns the specified String.

issues.description: The UML and solution define a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) that takes an Animal parameter. The template's Farm.java has singFarmSongVerse with the Animal parameter commented out (no parameter). This mismatch between the template and the described API can confuse students implementing singFarmSong(), since the helper signature in the template does not match the expected usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template Farm.java method signature: declare private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) so it matches the UML and solution. This ensures students can implement singFarmSong() by calling singFarmSongVerse(animal) without compilation friction.
